name: אֶלְיָסָף
summary: Borne by the leader of Gad in the wilderness, Eliasaph son of Deuel, who stood with Moses and Aaron to number Israel, brought Gad’s offering on the sixth day, and led Gad’s host when Israel set out from Sinai (Num 1:14; 7:42–47; 10:20); and by Eliasaph son of Lael, head of the fathers’ house of the Gershonites (Num 3:24). It is אֵל “God” and יָסָף, “he has added”: the thanks of parents given another child, as Rachel named Joseph saying “may Yahweh add to me another son” (Gen 30:24).

evidence.note: Over the host of the tribe of the sons of Gad, אֶלְיָסָף בֶּן־דְּעוּאֵל.
For Gad, Eliasaph son of Deuel, among the men who stood with Moses and Aaron.
The leader of the sons of Gad, Eliasaph son of רְעוּאֵל: the same man, his father’s name written with ר for ד.
On the sixth day, the leader of the sons of Gad brought his offering; the same at Num 7:47.
The leader of the fathers’ house of the Gershonite, אֶלְיָסָף בֶּן־לָאֵל.
Rachel calls her son יוֹסֵף, saying “יֹסֵף יַהְוֶה לִי another son”: a child is what God adds.
The name’s form, the qal perfect יָסָף, “he added”, as of Yahweh at Horeb.

note: BDB files the name under אֵל (a.dl.as, among the words of the elah entry, root אלה); it is linked here to the yasaph entry for its verb, יָסָף, the qal perfect “he has added”, so “God has added”. Punic has names of the same type, DN-ysp (Krahmalkov p. 210). The Gadite’s father is Deuel at Num 1:14; 7:42, 47; 10:20 and Reuel at Num 2:14 (ד and ר are easily confused); TIPNR makes Deuel and Reuel one person. Not to be confused with אֲבִיאָסָף / אֶבְיָסָף (Abiasaph, Exo 6:24; 1Ch 6:8), which BDB files under אבה and whose second part is אָסַף “gather”.
